classification.difficultyReason: Follow the taught logistic solution procedure, fit the rate using the second observation and square the resulting exponential factor to evaluate P(6).

content.prompt:
A herd satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP\left(1-\dfrac{P}{2000}\right)$ with $P(0)=250$ and $P(3)=500$.

Use $\dfrac{2000}{P(2000-P)}=\dfrac1P+\dfrac1{2000-P}$.

Find $k$ and $P(6)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{dt}{dP}&=\frac{2000}{kP(2000-P)}\\
\frac{dt}{dP}&=\frac1k\left(\frac1P+\frac1{2000-P}\right)\\
t&=\frac1k\left(\ln|P|-\ln|2000-P|\right)+D\\
\ln\left|\frac{P}{2000-P}\right|&=kt-kD\\
\frac{P}{2000-P}&=Ae^{kt}.
\end{align*}$$
Using $P(0)=250$:
$$\begin{align*}
A&=\frac{250}{1750}=\frac17\\
7P&=(2000-P)e^{kt}\\
P(7+e^{kt})&=2000e^{kt}\\
P(t)&=\frac{2000}{1+7e^{-kt}}.
\end{align*}$$
Using $P(3)=500$:
$$\begin{align*}
500&=\frac{2000}{1+7e^{-3k}}\\
1+7e^{-3k}&=4\\
e^{-3k}&=\frac37\\
k&=\frac13\ln\frac73.
\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}
e^{-6k}&=\left(\frac37\right)^2=\frac9{49}\\
P(6)&=\frac{2000}{1+7\cdot\frac9{49}}\\
P(6)&=875.
\end{align*}$$
